title: New year, new team, new turf: Moline Maroons ready to take the field - NewsBreak
text: MOLINE — A new season brings new excitement for the Moline Maroons, who are eager to showcase their skills on the newly installed turf at Browning Field. After battling through inconsistent grass conditions last year, players are ready to move faster, cut sharper, and fully reach their potential. “The grass last year was tough—it was an ankle-breaker,” said DeAnthony Simpson. “On turf, I can really play to my full potential. The cuts are going to be better, and even if it rains, it won’t slow us down.” Head Coach Mike Morrissey calls this the fastest team he’s ever coached, building off a successful 8-3 campaign in 2024. Speed and explosiveness start in the weight room with Coach Phelps, where players focus on leg workouts and timing drills that translate directly to their Wing T offense. Equally important, the Maroons’ success comes from their strong team chemistry. “You can’t just look at who’s a sophomore, junior, or senior—they all mesh together, encourage each other, and help pick each other up,” Morrissey said. Week one will put that bond to the test, as Moline travels six hours to Missouri to face Rockwood Summit. For many players, the overnight trip offers a unique experience reminiscent of college football, complete with a competitive atmosphere and pregame energy. “The goal is to give our kids a great experience while competing against a solid program,” Morrissey said. “They’ll get to see what it takes to prepare and perform at a high level.” With a combination of speed, teamwork, and determination, the Moline Maroons are ready to make a statement this season—on the turf, in the community, and in the record books.
